newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips quiet, SAX index eases 0.19 pts.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips quiet, SAX index eases 0.19 pts.

text.p: Slovak blue chips were quiet in thinner trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Wednesday, with a slight drop in VSZ steel shares pulling the SAX index down 0.19 points to 187.58.
Brokers said they expect the market to edge lower before prices finally begin to attract more foreign investors.

"The current low liquidity and low interst among investors may also be a result of the overall political instability in the country as well as some murky deals in the continuing privatisation," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings.
Overall volume decreased to 218,640 shares, from 261,263 stocks but only 813 shares traded the on the main BSE's floor. Turnover fell to 67.66 million crowns from 197.04 million.
Brokers said they expect foreign investors to focus mainly on stable issues, such as VSZ, plastic maker Plastika and drug producer Biotika, when they turn their attention to Slovak market.
VSZ dropped two crowns to close at 643, while oil refiner Slovnaft closed unchanged at 800. Oil and gas storage company Nafta did not trade.
